selectedBranch.description: Maintain a complete local-first Apache-2.0 analyzer, report, policy, adapter, and read-only CI loop without adding a hosted or account boundary.
selectedBranch.rationale: The scorecard has one bounded technical observation and seven not-observed dimensions, so no evidence justifies a new hosted, team, or collection boundary.

decision.rationale: The selected OSS-only branch keeps source processing and evidence review local; a future hosted or team proposal would change authorization, retention, tenancy, incident response, and operational ownership and must pass a new public RFC and ADR.
revisitTriggers: A public RFC proposes hosted source processing, accounts, team storage, or automatic collection.
The scorecard gains consented, reproducible privacy, security, capacity, funding, and adopter evidence for a materially different trust boundary.

assets.description: Caller-authorized repository source, configuration, package metadata, and Git history supplied to a local scan or revision comparison.
assets.integrityControl: Read source through the TypeScript parser and fixed Git/archive arguments; never import repository modules or run lifecycle scripts.
assets.retention: Source bodies remain in the caller repository or temporary revision tree and are not placed in canonical snapshots or reports.

assets.description: Canonical graph snapshots, evidence links, diagnostics, revision metadata, and diff classifications that reviewers rely on.
assets.integrityControl: Versioned schema validation, canonicalization, evidence invariants, deterministic serialization, and explicit unresolved diagnostics.
assets.retention: Retained only when the caller explicitly writes a local snapshot or report; no hosted history is created.

assets.description: Files outside the selected repository and the caller's dirty worktree or Git history.
assets.integrityControl: Repository-relative path validation, symlink checks, read-only Git commands, isolated temporary trees, and no checkout/reset/stash/clean operations.
assets.retention: No outside files are intentionally read; temporary revision trees are deleted in a finally path.

assets.description: Developer credentials and the read-only GitHub token context available to a pull-request runner.
assets.integrityControl: Local analysis has no credential loader; the workflow declares contents: read, persists no checkout credentials, and passes no secrets to the Action.
assets.retention: Credentials are not ingested into snapshots, reports, artifacts, or telemetry.

assets.description: Caller-selected JSON, Markdown, or self-contained HTML reports and the optional GitHub artifact copies.
assets.integrityControl: Escaped rendering, restrictive HTML CSP, output overwrite refusal by default, final-component no-follow open, and explicit upload opt-in.
assets.retention: Local retention is caller-controlled; Action artifacts default to seven days and can be disabled for sensitive repositories.

assets.description: Local and CI CPU, memory, file-count, archive, report-size, and wall-clock budgets.
assets.integrityControl: Fail-closed resource ceilings, cancellation signals, workflow timeouts, and bounded report cardinality.
assets.retention: Budget diagnostics are emitted only to the caller's local output or workflow log.

assets.description: The integrity of source distributions, dependency resolution, pinned workflow actions, and future release metadata.
assets.integrityControl: Committed lockfile, lifecycle-disabled installs, pinned Actions, dependency review, CodeQL, package dry-runs, and provenance checks.
assets.retention: No public npm release exists yet; future artifacts must retain checksums and provenance only.

actors.role: Maintainer or reviewer invoking the CLI on an authorized repository.
actors.startingAuthority: Can read the selected input and choose local output paths under their operating-system account.
canDo: Choose repository, refs, configuration, report format, and output path.
Read the resulting local graph, diff, policy, or runtime report.
cannotDo: Grant CARTOGRAPH a hosted account or remote storage capability.
Make the analyzer execute repository code or silently upload source.

actors.role: Author of source, configuration, Git history, package metadata, or local policy supplied as input.
actors.startingAuthority: Controls the input content and may intentionally provide hostile syntax, refs, paths, or metadata.
canDo: Influence parser inputs, Git refs, report text, and resource consumption within declared limits.
cannotDo: Escape validated roots, overwrite output by default, or turn diagnostics into canonical evidence.

actors.role: Untrusted contributor proposing a pull request that triggers the read-only Action or CI.
actors.startingAuthority: Controls fork branch content and pull-request text but does not control the base repository token or secrets.
canDo: Supply source and revision inputs to the pull-request workflow.
Cause bounded analysis failures or diagnostics.
cannotDo: Receive secrets, write repository contents, or choose pull_request_target execution.
Make the Action upload an artifact when upload-report is false.

actors.role: Ephemeral GitHub-hosted runner executing repository CI or the composite Action.
actors.startingAuthority: Receives workflow source and a least-privilege read token under GitHub's runner isolation assumptions.
canDo: Run pinned workflow steps, build the local package, and optionally upload report artifacts.
cannotDo: Authenticate a CARTOGRAPH tenant or persist a hosted graph database.
Override local parser, path, report, or resource controls.

actors.role: Maintainer, dependency publisher, or compromised package/action supply-chain participant.
actors.startingAuthority: May influence a reviewed dependency, pinned release process, or future artifact, subject to repository review and lockfile controls.
canDo: Propose dependency or release changes that enter review and validation.
cannotDo: Run install lifecycle scripts during CI's lifecycle-disabled install.
Publish a release through an unreviewed hosted service in the current scope.

actors.role: Private reporter of a suspected vulnerability or boundary failure.
actors.startingAuthority: Can provide a minimal authorized fixture or redacted reproduction through the private reporting channel.
canDo: Request maintainer triage and coordinated remediation.
cannotDo: Force public disclosure of secrets or source through the normal issue tracker.
Authorize a hosted or account-based product boundary.

dataFlows.data: Source text, compiler configuration, package metadata, and parser-visible syntax.
dataFlows.purpose: Build a canonical local graph snapshot.
dataFlows.retention: Source bodies are not serialized; only normalized relative evidence, hashes, nodes, edges, and diagnostics survive.
dataFlows.authorization: The operating-system caller must already be authorized to read the repository.
controls: Parser-only loading without imports or lifecycle execution.
Root-relative config and source selection.
Resource ceilings fail closed before partial output.

dataFlows.from: local Git repository and caller-supplied refs
dataFlows.to: fixed Git/archive subprocesses and isolated temporary tree
dataFlows.data: Validated commit IDs, tree contents, path history, and bounded archive bytes.
dataFlows.purpose: Compare exact revisions without changing the caller worktree.
dataFlows.retention: Materialized trees and partial archives are removed in a finally path after the comparison.
dataFlows.authorization: No remote fetch; the caller authorizes local Git read access.
controls: Argument-array subprocesses with no shell.
Ref and merge-base validation.
Archive, extracted-tree, memory, and wall-clock ceilings.

dataFlows.to: caller-selected JSON, Markdown, or self-contained HTML output
dataFlows.data: Versioned graph/diff records, relative evidence, diagnostics, and optional policy/ADR context.
dataFlows.purpose: Provide reviewable local evidence without source bodies or remote assets.
dataFlows.retention: The caller controls the output file; overwrite and symlink checks apply before writing.
dataFlows.authorization: The caller chooses the output path and must authorize any --force replacement.
controls: Escaped renderer output and restrictive HTML CSP.
No remote scripts, styles, fonts, or requests.
Report item and byte ceilings.

dataFlows.from: fork pull request and explicit base/head inputs
dataFlows.to: GitHub runner, local CARTOGRAPH build, and optional artifact store
dataFlows.data: Repository revisions, graph/diff JSON and HTML, policy result, and step summary.
dataFlows.purpose: Run an architecture diff in CI without write authority or source upload to CARTOGRAPH.
dataFlows.retention: Artifact upload is opt-in, defaults to seven days, and can be disabled for sensitive repositories; runner temp files are ephemeral.
dataFlows.authorization: GitHub supplies contents: read under pull_request; the composite Action receives no secrets.
controls: Pinned checkout/setup/upload actions.
persist-credentials: false in CI.
No pull_request_target and no workflow write permission.

dataFlows.to: data-only policy evaluator and optional Action exit status
dataFlows.data: Bounded selectors, modes, exception metadata, and diff references.
dataFlows.purpose: Report informational or enforcing architecture constraints without remote policy resolution.
dataFlows.retention: Policy input and result remain local or in the optional CI artifact selected by the caller.
dataFlows.authorization: The caller explicitly supplies the repository-relative policy path; no policy file grants authority.
controls: JSON-only local reader.
No commands, plugins, remote fetches, or authority escalation.
Stable exit codes and malformed-input failure.

dataFlows.from: explicit local GraphSnapshot, OTLP JSON, and span bindings
dataFlows.to: inert normalizer, bounded retention store, and local reconciliation report
dataFlows.data: Allowlisted trace identity and timing fields plus static/runtime classifications; arbitrary attributes and payloads are discarded.
dataFlows.purpose: Optional local experiment that compares declared runtime observations with static edges.
dataFlows.retention: Count, byte, time, and discard-after-read controls prevent implicit history; no collector or hosted retention exists.
dataFlows.authorization: The caller must provide all three local files; no listener, upload, or background process is started.
controls: Schema validation and explicit field-level redaction.
Fail-closed input and report budgets.
Uncertainty and provenance remain separate from static evidence.

dataFlows.from: reviewed source, lockfile, dependencies, and release configuration
dataFlows.to: local package rehearsal and future scoped release artifact
dataFlows.data: Build output, package manifest, checksums, SBOM/provenance metadata, and compatibility record.
dataFlows.purpose: Preserve reproducible distribution integrity without a current public release.
dataFlows.retention: No public package is released in this strategy branch; a future release retains artifact integrity metadata, not source inputs or telemetry.
dataFlows.authorization: Release publication remains an explicit maintainer operation outside the local analyzer's authority.
controls: Lifecycle-disabled install and lockfile.
Pinned workflow actions, dependency review, CodeQL, package contents checks, and provenance.
No automatic publish path in the current product.

tenancyAuthorization.operatorObligation: The caller must authorize repository reads, choose safe output locations, and treat reports as local artifacts; CARTOGRAPH does not authenticate callers or establish tenant isolation.

retention.rule: Do not copy source bodies into graph snapshots, reports, fixtures, scorecards, or telemetry.
retention.deletionOwner: Analyzer process and caller-managed repository permissions.

retention.rule: Delete materialized revision trees and partial archives after success or failure.
Retain a snapshot, diff, policy result, or report only when the caller explicitly writes it to a local path.
retention.deletionOwner: Local caller or repository workflow owner.

retention.rule: When upload-report is true, GitHub retains JSON/HTML reports for the configured one-to-ninety-day window; sensitive repositories can disable upload.
retention.deletionOwner: GitHub workflow owner and GitHub artifact retention control.

retention.rule: Optional runtime inputs are normalized, redacted, bounded by count/bytes/time, and explicitly discardable; no implicit history is retained.
Diagnostics and summaries follow the local terminal or GitHub workflow-log retention chosen by the caller; they are not copied to a CARTOGRAPH service.
retention.deletionOwner: Local operator or GitHub repository owner.

retention.rule: Do not collect hidden usage, source, account, retention, or background telemetry in the selected branch.
retention.deletionOwner: Not applicable because the collection is rejected.

resolvedQuestions.question: Does maxWallClockMs govern all Git work in a revision diff?
resolvedQuestions.resolution: No. It reaches materialization and analyzer resource options, while revision comparison and path-history calls receive only the cancellation signal and use the fixed subprocess timeout.

resolvedQuestions.question: Does maxReportItems cap every graph snapshot before a revision diff?
resolvedQuestions.resolution: No. Working-tree scan and final rendering assert limits, but materialized snapshots and the input schema do not apply the same cardinality assertion before diffing.

resolvedQuestions.question: Are hostile diff-snapshot files bounded by memory, time, and cancellation budgets before parsing?
resolvedQuestions.resolution: No. Two files are read concurrently with a 64 MiB input limit and renderer limits, but no explicit memory or analysis-time budget surrounds schema parsing and traversal.

resolvedQuestions.question: Does the composite Action enforce its documented repository-relative root and honor repository resource configuration?
resolvedQuestions.resolution: No. The Action passes the root input to diff without checking containment under GITHUB_WORKSPACE and exposes no config input, so the documented root-relative contract and repository resource settings remain consumer assumptions.

resolvedQuestions.question: Are runtime trace limits identical for CLI and library callers?
resolvedQuestions.resolution: No. The core policy permits up to 1 GiB input and has no explicit memory ceiling, while the CLI hard-validates a 64 MiB input ceiling; library callers remain a trusted boundary until the contracts converge.

resolvedQuestions.question: Is isolation automatic for every third-party adapter call?
resolvedQuestions.resolution: No. In-process runAdapter and isolated runAdapterIsolated are separate APIs; callers must select the permissioned child-process path for untrusted third-party adapters.

resolvedQuestions.question: What assumptions protect the privileged release workflow?
resolvedQuestions.resolution: The tag-triggered job intentionally grants contents, identity-token, and attestation write permissions; protected tags/main, trusted dependencies, and pinned actions must remain enforced before any public release.

incidentResponse.reporting: Use private GitHub vulnerability reporting when enabled or contact the maintainer privately; never place secrets or proprietary source in a public issue.
incidentResponse.detection: Reproduce with a minimal authorized or redacted fixture, the affected command/ref/configuration, and the local test or workflow evidence; absence of telemetry is intentional.
incidentResponse.containment: Disable the affected local command or Action upload, preserve the exact revision and redacted evidence, rotate any external token through its owner, and block a release until the boundary is reviewed.
incidentResponse.disclosure: Coordinate a practical disclosure and remediation plan privately; the unreleased project makes no fixed response-time or release-time promise.

supplyChain.residual: The compiler and npm dependency chain remain trusted dependencies; every future release or new adapter needs refreshed dependency, workflow, and ownership review.

abuseCases.attacker: Repository author supplying hostile TypeScript, package metadata, or lifecycle scripts.
abuseCases.entryPoint: Local scan, TypeScript project loading, or dependency directory in the selected root.
abuseCases.capabilityGain: If parser-only analysis imported or executed input, the attacker could run code with the caller or CI runner authority.
abuseCases.impact: Credential theft, local file disclosure, worktree tampering, or runner compromise.
controls: Parser APIs read syntax without importing modules.
CI installs with --ignore-scripts.
Negative offline fixtures assert no marker write or fetch.
abuseCases.mitigation: Keep the execution boundary enforced and require a new review for plugins, builds, or automatic binding.

abuseCases.attacker: Repository author controlling config paths, extends references, package maps, or symlinked files.
abuseCases.entryPoint: Root-relative config and TypeScript project resolution.
abuseCases.capabilityGain: A path-validation failure could read files outside the selected repository or temporary root.
abuseCases.impact: Disclosure of local source, credentials, or unrelated workspace data.
controls: Realpath containment checks.
Repository-relative schema paths.
Symlink and out-of-root project rejection.
abuseCases.mitigation: Preserve containment tests and review every new path-consuming adapter or exporter.

abuseCases.attacker: Repository author or fork contributor supplying an injection-shaped Git ref.
abuseCases.entryPoint: Revision comparison and archive subprocess arguments.
abuseCases.capabilityGain: If refs reached a shell or unsafe Git invocation, the attacker could execute commands or alter analysis targets.
abuseCases.impact: Command execution, wrong-revision evidence, or worktree damage.
controls: Fixed binaries and argument arrays with no shell.
Ref verification and exact commit resolution.
No fetch or worktree mutation.
abuseCases.mitigation: Keep the Git boundary read-only and fail closed for shallow, unrelated, or ambiguous histories.

abuseCases.attacker: Local caller, hostile repository path, or concurrent filesystem actor controlling an output location.
abuseCases.capabilityGain: A write-path failure could overwrite a user file or follow a symlink into a protected location.
controls: Overwrite refusal without --force.
Final and parent symlink preflight.
Final-component no-follow open and private file permissions.
abuseCases.mitigation: Retain the documented race limitation and do not claim concurrent filesystem changes are fully prevented.

abuseCases.attacker: Repository author supplying oversized, recursive, ambiguous, or high-cardinality input.
abuseCases.entryPoint: Source scan, Git archive, runtime trace import, policy evaluation, or report rendering.
abuseCases.capabilityGain: A missing budget could consume unbounded CPU, memory, disk, or CI time.
abuseCases.impact: Local denial of service or exhausted shared runner capacity.
controls: Source, archive, extracted-tree, memory, report, and wall-clock ceilings.
Cancellation and cleanup in finally paths.
CI timeout.
abuseCases.mitigation: Keep each new adapter and report surface within the declared ceilings and add a bounded regression fixture before expansion.

abuseCases.attacker: Repository author controlling names, diagnostics, evidence labels, or policy text.
abuseCases.entryPoint: Markdown or self-contained HTML report rendering.
abuseCases.capabilityGain: An escaping failure could execute markup or request remote resources in a reviewer's browser.
abuseCases.impact: Local disclosure, phishing, or script execution in the report context.
controls: Escape repository-controlled text.
No repository-provided HTML or remote assets.
Restrictive HTML CSP and static report tests.
abuseCases.mitigation: Treat any new renderer or report embedding as a separate security review.

abuseCases.attacker: Untrusted fork contributor modifying source or workflow-adjacent inputs in a pull request.
abuseCases.entryPoint: pull_request CI and the composite Action.
abuseCases.capabilityGain: A workflow permission or event mistake could expose a token or permit repository writes.
abuseCases.impact: Repository mutation, secret theft, or supply-chain compromise.
controls: pull_request event, contents: read, no secrets, persist-credentials: false, pinned actions, and no pull_request_target.
abuseCases.mitigation: Re-run the fork smoke and workflow policy tests for every permission or event change.

abuseCases.attacker: Compromised dependency, action ref, maintainer credential, or future package publication path.
abuseCases.entryPoint: Install, build, workflow action, package rehearsal, or release publication.
abuseCases.capabilityGain: A supply-chain compromise could alter the analyzer or distribute a malicious artifact.
abuseCases.impact: Developer or CI compromise and integrity loss for graph evidence.
controls: Lockfile, lifecycle-disabled install, pinned actions, dependency review, CodeQL, package contents checks, and provenance.
abuseCases.mitigation: Require a release-specific dependency, signing, identity, and incident-response review before any public package or hosted worker.

abuseCases.attacker: Local input author supplying malicious OTLP records or sensitive free-text attributes.
abuseCases.capabilityGain: A normalization or retention failure could expose source, credentials, or personal data in a report or long-lived history.
abuseCases.impact: Sensitive-data disclosure or misleading runtime evidence.
controls: No collector or listener.
Allowlisted fields, redaction, count/byte/time bounds, explicit discard, and uncertainty labels.
abuseCases.mitigation: Keep runtime reconciliation outside the default CLI/report loop until the trace safety and retention gates are re-reviewed.

blockingMitigations.requirement: Repository source, configuration, and traces remain inert local data; no imports, lifecycle scripts, plugins, collectors, or hidden network requests run.
blockingMitigations.blockingReason: Breaking this boundary would grant repository-controlled code or data a new caller or runner capability.

blockingMitigations.requirement: Validate repository-relative paths and reject traversal, archived symlinks, output symlinks, and unsafe parents before writing.
blockingMitigations.blockingReason: Path escape or unsafe output could disclose or destroy files outside the selected local boundary.

blockingMitigations.requirement: Resolve refs locally with fixed argument arrays, materialize isolated trees, and never mutate the caller worktree.
blockingMitigations.blockingReason: Git argument or worktree mutation would turn untrusted history into command or data-loss authority.

blockingMitigations.requirement: Preserve source, archive, memory, report, trace, and wall-clock ceilings with cleanup on cancellation or failure.
blockingMitigations.blockingReason: An unbounded local or CI workload could deny service to the caller or shared runner.

blockingMitigations.requirement: Reports contain escaped local evidence only, no source bodies or absolute paths, no remote assets, and a restrictive CSP.
blockingMitigations.blockingReason: A report is opened by a reviewer and must not become a browser execution or disclosure boundary.

blockingMitigations.requirement: Fork pull requests run under pull_request with contents: read, no secrets, pinned actions, and no write-capable target event.
blockingMitigations.blockingReason: A workflow permission mistake could grant untrusted fork content repository or secret authority.

blockingMitigations.requirement: Any hosted, account, team, automatic-binding, or provider expansion requires a public RFC, refreshed evidence, privacy/security review, cost model, claims audit, capacity charter, and separate ADR.
blockingMitigations.blockingReason: A new trust boundary would introduce authorization, tenancy, retention, incident-response, and operational ownership that local-only controls do not cover.

rejectedDataCollection.item: Uploading repository source, graph snapshots, or raw issue bodies to a hosted service.
rejectedDataCollection.rationale: The local loop is complete without source transfer, and proprietary architecture input cannot be made a prerequisite for use.

rejectedDataCollection.item: Requiring an account, tenant, workspace, or organizational history service.
rejectedDataCollection.rationale: No supported product operation needs identity or multi-tenant storage; adding it now would create an unearned authorization boundary.

rejectedDataCollection.item: Background usage telemetry, source collection, retention measurement, or silent network requests.
rejectedDataCollection.rationale: The scorecard and feedback contracts require manual public or consented aggregate evidence and prohibit private telemetry.

rejectedDataCollection.item: An OTLP listener, automatic trace collector, or implicit runtime history store.
rejectedDataCollection.rationale: Runtime reconciliation is an explicit local experiment with bounded input and no collector; automatic binding remains outside the product boundary.

rejectedDataCollection.item: Sending source, issue text, credentials, or uncertain fields to a model provider or other external processor.
rejectedDataCollection.rationale: The provider boundary is design-only and disabled; a future adapter needs consent, allowlists, retention/deletion controls, and independent red-team review.

residualRisks.risk: Static analysis can miss dynamic JavaScript behavior and therefore cannot prove complete architectural truth.
residualRisks.impact: A reviewer may under-estimate an unmodeled relationship if diagnostics and limitations are ignored.
residualRisks.treatment: Keep unknowns and confidence visible, preserve unsupported diagnostics, and do not convert missing evidence into a claim.

residualRisks.risk: The TypeScript compiler, ts-morph, npm dependencies, and GitHub runner remain trusted computing dependencies.
residualRisks.impact: A compromised dependency or runner could alter analysis or expose caller data within its existing authority.
residualRisks.treatment: Keep lockfile, dependency review, pinned Actions, CodeQL, lifecycle-disabled installs, provenance, and release review current.

residualRisks.risk: Output preflight and final-component no-follow semantics do not claim race-free protection from concurrent filesystem changes.
residualRisks.impact: A concurrent local actor could still change a path after preflight and before a write.
residualRisks.treatment: Keep the race limitation explicit; use trusted output directories and avoid treating the CLI as a hostile multi-process file server.

residualRisks.risk: The read-only Action still executes on a GitHub-hosted runner whose isolation and artifact controls are external assumptions.
residualRisks.impact: A runner or artifact-service compromise could expose the inputs or reports already available to that workflow.
residualRisks.owner: GitHub workflow owner and GitHub service.
residualRisks.treatment: Keep permissions minimal, uploads opt-in and short-lived, and local execution the complete product path; review any hosted expansion separately.

provenance.source: CARTOGRAPH repository-authored strategy privacy and security review fixture
provenance.reference: M-009 strategy-branch privacy and security review; F-002 threat model; M-005 scorecard; M-006 ADR
provenance.transformation: The fixture turns the supported local CLI, read-only Action, optional local trace experiment, release controls, and explicit rejected collection into a digestable public review without source bodies, secrets, private records, or telemetry.
